newsitem.title: UK: CME signs clearing, trading link with MATIF, SBF.
newsitem.headline: CME signs clearing, trading link with MATIF, SBF.

text.p: The Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) signed an agreement on Thursday with France's MATIF and the SBF-Paris Bourse to link up clearing systems.
According to the deal, CME will swap its Clearing 21 system in return for the SBF-Paris Bourse's NSC electronic trading system, officials said in a signing ceremony in London.
The signing was made to coincide with the International Derivatives Conference in London.
Officials said Clearing 21, which is a real-time matching and clearing system for futures and options, would be expanded for clearing equity securities and cash market instruments.
Similarly, the SBF-Paris Bourse NSC system used for equity securities and equity options would be modified to also trade futures and options on futures.
Separately, heads of the three exchanges also signed a letter of intent to license and market the entire package of trading and clearing systems to other potential exchanges.
The new system is expected to be implemented in the second half of 1998.
The new system, which was expected to halve trading costs in five years, would serve as the new operating system for GLOBEX, the after-hours electronic system of the CME and Matif.

Asked whether a project for a similar link-up between CME and the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) was moving forward, the CME Chairman Jack Sandner said, "We're moving along. We're analysing the hardware now."
